title: -An verb forms
summary: The suffix -an (or -han): places like aklátan, and passive verbs like basáhan, lagyán and buksán
goals: Know the jobs the suffix -an does: a place, a passive action, size and quality
Build the infinitive, imperative, past, present and future of an -an verb
Recognise the irregular -an verbs (lagyán, buksán, hipan…)
Change an -um- or mag- sentence into an -an sentence

blocks.t: **-an** is a **suffix**: it is attached to the **end** of a root word. The new -an word can do several different jobs.

head: Job
Root
-an word
rows: [[gúpítan|noun]] (a place where they cut: a barber shop or beauty salon)
An **action** in the passive form, like the -in verbs
[[sulatan|pred]] (to write, or the act of writing)
blocks.title: One suffix, several jobs
What this lesson focuses on
blocks.t: The book says this lesson focuses on **how -an words are formed**, more than on what they mean in context.

blocks.title: Like -in, but different
blocks.t: In Lesson 15 the **-in** verbs were **passive**: the thing acted upon became the subject. The **-an** verbs are passive too, but the subject is usually the **person or place** the action is aimed at (*to read **to someone***, *to write **on** the book*). Section 6 shows this.
Two forms of the suffix are used. Which one depends on how the root word **ends**. (The glottal catch is the stress written with a circumflex ^, from Lesson 2.)

blocks.title: Same rule as Lesson 15
blocks.t: This is the same idea as **-in** and **-hin** in Lesson 15: the extra **h** comes in after a vowel that has no glottal catch.
Like the -in verbs, an -an verb has an **infinitive**, an **imperative** and three tenses. The book calls these forms the **derivatives** of the verb.

blocks.t: With roots beginning with the consonants **l, w** and **y**, the infix **-in-** becomes the prefix **ni-**. You met this in Lesson 15 (lutò → nilutò). So lagay gives **nilagyán**, not *linagyán*.

blocks.title: The pattern
items: **Infinitive and imperative** look the same: root + **-an** or **-han**.
**Past**: **in-** is added (inalisán), or **-in-** goes after the first letter (bínasáhan), or **ni-** for lagay (nilagyán). Nothing is doubled.
**Present**: like the past, with the **first syllable doubled**.
**Future**: the **first syllable doubled**, with no in-, -in- or ni-.
-an or -han stays on the end in **every** form.

blocks.title: Examples of irregular -an verbs
Other changes too
blocks.t: Some irregular verbs change in other ways as well. In the last example, **hipan** (from **hihip**, blow), the second syllable **hi** is deleted altogether: *hihipan* → **hipan**. Compare each verb with its bracketed form to see what changed.

blocks.title: Two kinds of washing
blocks.t: **labhán** is to wash **clothes**; **hugásan** is to wash something that is **not** clothes.
To change an **-um-** or **mag-** sentence (Lesson 14) into an **-an** sentence, follow these guidelines.
I. Without a direct object

If the -um- or mag- sentence has **no direct object**, the **indirect object** (introduced by **para kay**, **kay**, **para sa** or **sa**) or the **place** (introduced by **sa**) becomes the **subject** of the -an sentence. The **doer** then takes a possessive article: **ni** or **ng**.

blocks.title: -um- sentence → -an sentence
blocks.note: The child wrote on the book.

blocks.title: The pronouns change too
blocks.t: The indirect object **sa ákin** in the mag- sentence becomes the subject **ako** in the -an sentence, and the doer **ka** becomes **mo** (see Lesson 6 on personal and demonstrative pronouns).
II. With a direct object

If the -um- or mag- sentence **has a direct object** (the noun or pronoun that receives the action), that object is preceded by the possessive article **ng** in the -an sentence. The indirect object and the doer follow rule I.

You read to me a story. (-an)

blocks.t: III. Without -in- verbs
When an -um- or mag- verb has **no -in- form**, the **direct object** becomes the **subject** in the -an sentence.

blocks.title: No -in- form: the object becomes the subject
Summary
items: The **doer** takes the possessive form: **ng batà**, **ni** + name, **mo**, **ko**, **ninyó**.
The person or place the action is aimed at becomes the **subject** (ang, or a pronoun like ako).
No -in- form? Then the direct object becomes the subject (Buksán mo ang pintô).

blocks.title: Spelling
blocks.t: The book prints the subject as **akó** in *Basáhan mo akó* and as **ako** in *Basáhan mo ako ng kuwento*.

blocks.t: The book points out that **Pakinggán** is a **pa- + -an** verb: it has a prefix **pa-** as well as the suffix -an.

blocks.title: Remember
items: -an after a consonant or a glottal catch (alisán, hingán); -han after a vowel without one (basáhan, samáhan).
Tenses: alisán / inalisán / ináalisán / áalisán and basáhan / bínasáhan / binábasahan / bábasahan.
Irregular verbs drop the second vowel of the root: lagyán, buksán, labhán. Roots with l, w, y take ni- (nilagyán).
In an -an sentence the doer takes ng / ni / mo / ko, and the person or place the action is aimed at becomes the subject.

exercises.q: What does aklátan mean?
exercises.explain: An -an word can be a place linked to the root: aklát (book) → aklátan (library).

exercises.q: What is gúpítan?
options: a barber shop or beauty salon
exercises.answer: a barber shop or beauty salon
exercises.explain: From gupít (to cut): a place where they cut.

exercises.q: Putikan (from putik, mud) describes…
exercises.explain: The book gives -an for size (damihan) and quality (putikan).

exercises.q: Which suffix goes on a root that ends in a vowel WITHOUT a glottal catch, like sama?
exercises.explain: -Han is the variant form used after a vowel without a glottal catch: samáhan.

exercises.q: Hingî ends in a vowel WITH a glottal catch. Which suffix does it take?
exercises.explain: -An goes after consonants and after vowels with a glottal catch.

exercises.q: Which form of alís means "was/were removed"?
exercises.explain: Past: prefix in- + root word + -an.

exercises.q: Which form of alís means "will be removed"?
exercises.explain: Future: duplicate first syllable + root word + -an.

exercises.q: Which form of basa means "is/are being read to someone"?
exercises.explain: Present: infix -in- after the first letter, plus a doubled first syllable.

exercises.q: Why is the past of lagay nilagyán and not with -in- inside?
options: The root begins with l, so -in- becomes the prefix ni-
The root ends in a glottal catch
exercises.answer: The root begins with l, so -in- becomes the prefix ni-
exercises.explain: With l, w and y, the infix -in- becomes the prefix ni- (Lesson 15).

exercises.q: What happens to the root in most irregular -an verbs?
options: The second vowel of the root is dropped
exercises.answer: The second vowel of the root is dropped
exercises.explain: labahan → labhán, bukasan → buksán.

exercises.q: In which irregular verb is a whole syllable (hi) deleted?
exercises.explain: From hihip (blow): hihipan → hipan.

exercises.q: Which verb is for washing CLOTHES?
exercises.explain: Hugásan is to wash something that is not clothes.

exercises.q: In "Sinulátan ng batà ang aklát", what is the subject?
exercises.explain: The place (sa aklát) in the -um- sentence becomes the subject (ang aklát).

exercises.q: In an -an sentence, the doer is preceded by…
exercises.explain: Sinulátan ng batà ang aklát.

exercises.q: How does "Magbasá ka sa ákin" become an -an sentence?
exercises.explain: Sa ákin becomes the subject ako, and ka becomes mo.

exercises.q: How does "Magbukás ka ng pintô" become an -an sentence?
exercises.explain: With no -in- form, the direct object becomes the subject.

exercises.q: In an -an sentence that keeps a direct object, the direct object is preceded by…
exercises.explain: Basáhan mo ako ng kuwento.

exercises.q: In "Inalisán ng babáe ng pagkain ang anák", the subject is…
exercises.explain: This is the book's own worked example.

exercises.q: What is the active form of "Inalisán ng babáe ng pagkain ang anák"?
options: Nag-alís ang babáe ng pagkain sa anák.
Nag-alís ng babáe ang pagkain sa anák.
Nag-alís ang babáe ang pagkain ng anák.
exercises.answer: Nag-alís ang babáe ng pagkain sa anák.
exercises.explain: The doer takes ang, the food keeps ng, and the child takes sa.

exercises.q: "Nilabhán ng katúlong ko ang áming damít" means…

exercises.explain: Nilabhán is the past (ni- + labhán).

exercises.answer: I will read a nice story to my father.

recap: -an makes places (aklátan, gúpítan), passive actions (sulatan), size (damihan) and quality (putikan).
-an after a consonant or a glottal catch; -han after a vowel without one (basáhan, samáhan).
Tenses: alisán / inalisán / ináalisán / áalisán; basáhan / bínasáhan / binábasahan / bábasahan; lagyán / nilagyán / nilálagyán / lálagyán.
Irregular -an verbs drop the second vowel of the root: labhán, sundán, buksán, tingnán; hipan drops a whole syllable.
-an sentences: verb + doer (ng, ni, mo, ko) + subject. The indirect object or place becomes the subject; a direct object keeps ng.
